name: Box Turn (forward half)
notes: Owner's description: the basic waltz step, counts 1-2-3, a quarter turn clockwise while progressing forward; lead starts forward on the right foot, the feet close on 3, and the turn is felt mostly on 2. Usually followed by Box Turn (backward half). Step sizes and rise are assumptions the owner accepted for now (2026-11-16): 0.5 forward, then the left foot lands 0.4 beyond the right in the turned frame; no rise. The whole quarter turn is placed on step 2. Step 2 is 'side' in the turned frame: the lead's left foot travels from beside the right heel to 0.4 past the right foot (0.9 forward and 0.2 right of where it was, measured from his facing before the turn). The lead goes forward on step 2, so the couple turns round the follow, who is on the inside of the turn (the default turning centre, 2026-11-17), and a `both` turning step is written as the centre's step: 0.4 forward and 0.5 right as he'd say it, which for her is 0.4 back and 0.5 to her left, a 0.64 stride. He travels round her, 0.92, landing where he did before the turning centre was added. Exempt from the "partner spacing" and "crossed feet" checks (added 2026-11-16, still needed 2026-11-17): on count 2 the follow's right foot passes over the lead's standing right foot, which after count 1 sits between her feet in the offset hold, and her feet cross briefly. Splitting the turn between counts 1 and 2, or a curved path for her, is left for the figure clean-up. Remove skipChecks once it's fixed. Turn timing from the book (2026-11-17, a box-step study card: the partner going forward turns 1/8 between 1 and 2 and 1/8 between 2 and 3; the partner going back turns 1/4 between 1 and 2, "body turns less", and the body completes the turn on 3): the bodies turn 1/8 right on count 2 and 1/8 on the close, and the follow, going back on the inside of the turn, points the foot a further 1/8 on count 2 (`pointing`), so her feet make the whole quarter between 1 and 2. The close's turn is carried back into count 2's foot placement, so the feet land exactly where they did with the whole quarter on count 2.
